text:
nina: heads-up — saw tenant-level starvation in staging this morning with the continuous-batcher enabled. lots of 1-2 token requests from the mobile client piled up and long requests later were delayed ~150-300ms beyond expected.
jorge: ugh. do you have a repro or logs?
nina: repro attached. pattern: high prefix-cache hit rate, short-latency requests (<=3 tokens), plus one or two long streaming jobs. short requests kept coalescing and filling microbatches, but they never matured into a dispatch because the batcher kept waiting for >batch_size or deadline. long jobs then got starved when the runtime picked a nearly-full microbatch that had no long job kvs.
cheng: can you paste the relevant log snippet?
nina: sure

```
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] tenant=acme req=0x1 size=2 enqueued
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] tenant=acme req=0x2 size=2 enqueued
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] tenant=acme req=0x3 size=128 enqueued (stream)
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] batcher: microbatch 0x10 waiting deadline=40ms
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] microbatch 0x10 dispatched (only small requests) latency=360ms
[2026-03-20T08:12:11Z] req=0x3 started (delayed due to KV warmup)
```
beau: sounds like deadline-driven coalesce with naive size heuristics. we treat short reqs as low-cost, but they add scheduling noise.
kim: we saw similar on canary but blamed it on prefetch/kvcache eviction order. two knobs we can tweak: 1) per-tenant time-slicing (guarantee X ms reserved for long inflight), 2) preemptive slice eviction when a long request is waiting.
jorge: i'd rather not add heavy preemption in the fast path. option: change admission to allow a "latency-prioritized" lane — small fraction of slots reserved for long requests. basically a token bucket per tenant for heavy requests.
cheng: sketch: maintain two queues per tenant: small and large. admission: if large-queue non-empty and large-reserve>0 dispatch from large until reserve drained, else batch from small. reserve refills at R tokens/sec.
nina: that could work. edge case: if large jobs are rare but huge, we might underutilize GPUs if reserve sits idle. need fallback: allow borrowing from small when utilization < 60%.
beau: agree; also consider extending deadline logic: instead of waiting for batch_size we use adaptive windows based on observed size distribution. e.g. if 80% of recent requests are size<=4 then shorten window to 12ms.
kim: also worth instrumenting token-affinity: prefer combining requests that share prefix KV to reduce KV warmup costs. logs show the long job suffered KV warmup after many small ones.
jorge: operationally: add metrics for "long-request-wait-time", "reserve-utilization", and per-tenant dispatch fairness. agree on a short experiment: implement 2-queue lanes + 10% reserve for large, borrow when GPU util < 55%. canary in staging, measure p95 for long jobs.
nina: I can prototype the admission change today. will push an opt-in flag and a small dashboard.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: batcher/opt-in/large-reserve -> staging at 2026-03-20T14:00:00Z :rocket:
cheng: thanks. follow-up: we should write an RFC if the experiment shows >30% p95 improvement for long requests without degrading small-request p50.
beau: +1. also add a simple simulator for mixed workloads — will help tune reserve size.
nina: cool. I'll post results here and attach sim runs. :thumbsup:
